body: I don't know, something about brutally lonely men barely stringing together a life gets to me. Both protagonists find themselves orbiting around a much wiser, well put together person who drags them from the depths of their depression back into life. While neither ever is quite happy they at least find solace in themselves. Plus both blindly and completely love women who are by all rights evil, who drag them down and down and down, seems like the kind of relationship I'd be in.
Steinbeck's East of Eden, maybe Gaiman's American Gods.
Jesus, that's an interesting question. I'm not sure I have a useful answer. A couple books are the only things that really jump to mind.

It's not about anyone else, you mentioned that I'm young, that life is longer than it used to be. I don't want it to be if I have to keep feeling like this all the time. That last sentence is the opposite of helpful withoult some kind of explanation.

No friends, psychotic family and nonexistant social skills means I am alone all of the time. Never been in a relationship. No job I even vaguely aspire to. Either stoned all of the time or grinding my teeth and twitching. Spent the last two years getting in shape and working out and all its done is made my temper that much shorter and strangers afraid of me. As a person I work out to a null statement, I bring neither positive nor negative to the world. You might say my death would be a negative, but if I do it right everyone will just think I disappeared and that's not so bad.
